run.question:
Alertmanager alert KubePodNotReady (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 since 2026-11-25T21:38:44Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is firing for a pod that never became schedulable. Pod otel-demo/payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 (created 2026-11-25T21:37:58Z) is Pending with PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable, and the scheduler reports '0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 1 node(s) were unschedulable'. The pod template behind it (ReplicaSet payment-7b79bbd6dc, created 21:37:41Z) carries nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=kind-environment-worker, and node kind-environment-worker was made unschedulable at 2026-11-25T21:37:58Z (spec.unschedulable=true, taint node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule, added by field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' plus kube-controller-manager; kubelet event NodeNotSchedulable at 21:38:00Z). The same template's first pod, payment-7b79bbd6dc-pbxr4, had scheduled onto that node at 21:37:41Z while it was still schedulable and is Ready, is the single endpoint of the payment Service, logs no error lines, and payment spans show only STATUS_CODE_UNSET statuses; the Deployment therefore reports 1 of 2 replicas available (Available=False, MinimumReplicasUnavailable). So the alert reflects a scheduling failure caused by the cordoned node that the workload is pinned to, not a failing payment process; who or what cordoned the node, and the intent of the 21:37:41Z deployment update by the same client field manager, are not determinable from the available sources.

claims.text: Pod otel-demo/payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 (created 2026-11-25T21:37:58Z, owner ReplicaSet payment-7b79bbd6dc) is phase Pending with no containerStatuses and condition PodScheduled=False/reason Unschedulable: '0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 1 node(s) were unschedulable. preemption: 0/3 nodes are available: 3 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

For pod payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4, kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Pending"}=1 at every 30s sample from 21:38:30Z through 21:43:30Z (first returned sample 21:38:30Z, source_end_at 21:43:30Z) while phase Running=0, i.e. the pod stayed Pending for the observed interval.

Two Warning FailedScheduling events exist for pod payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 (first 2026-11-25T21:37:58Z, last 2026-11-25T21:43:03Z) with the same '0/3 nodes are available ...' message, and Normal SuccessfulCreate events show ReplicaSet payment-7b79bbd6dc created pod payment-7b79bbd6dc-pbxr4 at 21:37:41Z and pod payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 at 21:37:58Z.

Node kind-environment-worker is cordoned: spec.unschedulable=true and taint node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule with timeAdded 2026-11-25T21:37:58Z (in addition to the pre-existing itbench.io/sandbox=true:NoSchedule taint); its metadata.managedFieldsSummary shows Update by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 2026-11-25T21:37:58Z and Update by kube-controller-manager at the same time, and the node stays Ready=True with sufficient memory, disk and PID.
A Normal event reported by kubelet on kind-environment-worker at 2026-11-25T21:38:00Z reads 'Node kind-environment-worker status is now: NodeNotSchedulable'.

The payment Deployment's current pod template pins pods to one node with nodeSelector {kubernetes.io/hostname: kind-environment-worker}; the cluster has exactly three nodes (kind-environment-control-plane, kind-environment-worker, kind-environment-worker2), and the pod's FailedScheduling message states that one node failed its node affinity/selector, one had an untolerated taint and one was unschedulable — so the only node matching the selector is the cordoned worker node.

Deployment payment is at generation 3 with spec.replicas=2 and status readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1, unavailableReplicas=1, condition Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable (lastTransitionTime 2026-11-25T21:37:58Z); its managedFieldsSummary shows helm Apply at 2026-11-25T21:30:17Z and Update by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 2026-11-25T21:37:41Z.

The nodeSelector is new to the payment pod template: ReplicaSet payment-fc757bc4c (created 2026-11-25T21:30:18Z, now 0 replicas) has nodeSelector null, while ReplicaSet payment-7b79bbd6dc (created 2026-11-25T21:37:41Z, 2 replicas) has nodeSelector {kubernetes.io/hostname: kind-environment-worker}; Deployment events show ScalingReplicaSet for the new RS 0->1 and the old RS 1->0 at 21:37:41Z and for the new RS 1->2 at 21:37:58Z, the same second the pod was created and the node was cordoned.

kube_pod_status_ready shows pod payment-7b79bbd6dc-pbxr4 with condition="true"=1 at every 60s sample from 21:38:51Z to 21:43:51Z (and condition="false"=0), and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="payment"}=1 at every sample from 21:30:44Z to 21:43:44Z.

The surviving payment replica is serving: Service payment (ClusterIP 10.96.160.246, selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment) has one Endpoints address, pod payment-7b79bbd6dc-pbxr4 on node kind-environment-worker (10.244.2.19), and that pod's container logs for 21:37:41Z-21:43:51Z contain no error lines (only node startup DeprecationWarning/MetadataLookupWarning lines).

For service_name="payment", the only status_code series returned by sum by (status_code) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"}[5m])) over 21:38:51Z-21:43:51Z was STATUS_CODE_UNSET at roughly 1.05-1.46 spans/s; no ERROR-coded status_code series appeared in that view (span counts are not request counts and STATUS_CODE_UNSET does not mean success).

Deployment payment is the only otel-demo Deployment with a nodeSelector and the only one with replicas=2; the other 25 otel-demo Deployments have nodeSelector null and replicas=1, and cluster-wide the only non-running/non-ready workload pods found were payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 (Pending, otel-demo), prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0 (Running, ContainersNotReady, itbench-observability) and the completed job pod clickhouse-init-77hsv.

The KubePodNotReady alerting rule (expression requiring phase Pending|Unknown, or Running with ready!=1, for 300s) is in state firing for pod otel-demo/payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 with activeAt 2026-11-25T21:38:44Z; the same rule is also firing for the unrelated pod itbench-observability/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0 with activeAt 2026-11-25T21:27:44Z.

A flagd fault-injection flag on the payment service is not the explanation: ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo has every flag at defaultVariant "off", including paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, and the pod's problem is scheduling (Pending with no container), not a payment handler failure.

Causal chain: node kind-environment-worker was cordoned at 21:37:58Z, and because Deployment payment's pod template (written 21:37:41Z, the same second the first pod of that template scheduled onto the still-schedulable worker) requires that exact node and the Deployment then ran two replicas, the second replica payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 had no eligible node and stayed Pending, which is what the KubePodNotReady alert reports; the template's single-node pinning is a contributing configuration that removes any fallback node.

The 21:37:41Z update of Deployment payment (client field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator', introducing nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=kind-environment-worker) and the 21:37:58Z cordon of kind-environment-worker (same client field manager) may be two steps of one deliberate fault-injection or maintenance action, but the evidence does not identify the actor or its intent.

gaps: Who or what cordoned kind-environment-worker at 2026-11-25T21:37:58Z is unknown: the node's managedFieldsSummary names only the client field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' (with kube-controller-manager adding the unschedulable taint), and the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no audit trail or actor identity could be checked.

The 21:37:41Z update of Deployment payment by the same client field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' (pod template gaining the single-node nodeSelector, with the replicas=2 state observed afterwards) cannot be attributed to a named actor or intent, and the order in which replicas and template were written is not shown, since managedFieldsSummary carries only each manager's last write time.

No trace-level review of payment was possible: the traces_search call for service payment over 21:38:44Z-21:43:51Z returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE (485 spans, result not adopted, not citable), so individual payment traces and their error tags were not examined; only the aggregated span status_code series were read.
kube_pod_status_ready returned no series for pod payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 (only for pbxr4 and the deleted fc757bc4c-5pgtw), so that pod's readiness condition value is unknown rather than zero.

The attempt to list customresourcedefinitions to look for chaos/fault-injection controllers returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE and was not adopted, so the presence of chaos tooling capable of cordoning nodes was not established.

Other changes during the window are not tied to this alert by evidence and were not investigated further: metrics-server pods in kube-system were stopped/recreated (Killing events 2026-11-25T20:50:01Z and 2026-11-25T21:19:02Z), and pod itbench-observability/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0 is ContainersNotReady with its own KubePodNotReady active since 21:27:44Z.
next_steps: Check the cluster audit log or the operator/chaos framework's records for the identity behind the field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' that set spec.unschedulable on kind-environment-worker and updated Deployment payment at 2026-11-25T21:37:41Z-21:37:58Z.

If the cordon was intended, uncordon kind-environment-worker (or remove the single-node nodeSelector / add capacity on a second node) so the second payment replica can schedule; confirm with kubectl get pod payment-7b79bbd6dc-bt5b4 that it leaves Pending.

Review why Deployment payment was given nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=kind-environment-worker together with replicas=2, since that combination leaves the workload one cordoned node away from an unschedulable replica.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
